“At Global Academy of Technology, the MBA program is envisioned as a launchpad for future business leaders who can navigate complexity, drive innovation, and create meaningful impact. Our focus is on shaping agile, analytical, and ethically grounded professionals through a curriculum that blends academic rigor, industry relevance, and data-driven decision-making. 
 Through outcome-based education, analytics-led specializations, experiential learning, and strong industry engagement, we prepare students to lead with confidence and clarity in a dynamic global economy. The MBA at GAT empowers learners to think strategically, act responsibly, and evolve into transformative leaders of tomorrow.”

“At Global Academy of Technology, academic excellence is driven by relevance, rigor, and continuous improvement. As Associate Dean – Academics, my focus is on strengthening a forward-looking curriculum that integrates Outcome-Based Education, industry alignment, and experiential learning.

Through structured curricula, industry-led courses, internships, capstone projects, advanced laboratories, and online certifications, we aim to create a holistic and future-ready learning ecosystem. Our emphasis on clearly defined learning outcomes and measurable skill development ensures that students graduate as competent, ethical, and industry-ready professionals. Together, we strive to uphold quality standards and prepare learners to succeed in a dynamic engineering landscape.”

“At Global Academy of Technology, quality and excellence form the foundation of all academic and institutional practices. The IQAC is committed to fostering a culture of continuous improvement through reflective teaching, research-driven curriculum design, and robust assessment frameworks.

We emphasize evidence-based decision-making, collaboration, and innovation to ensure our programs meet national and international quality benchmarks. By empowering faculty, strengthening academic processes, and aligning learning outcomes with global standards, we strive to enhance student success and institutional growth. I encourage all stakeholders to actively engage in quality initiatives as we collectively build a future-ready, learner-centric institution.”

“At Global Academy of Technology, we are committed to nurturing students not only academically, but also personally and professionally. The Office of Student Affairs strives to create a supportive, inclusive campus where every student feels valued, mentored, and empowered to succeed.We believe holistic development—combining academic excellence, wellbeing, leadership, and strong values—is key to thriving in a dynamic world. Through continuous mentoring, student engagement, and meaningful alumni connections, we prepare our students to grow with confidence, integrity, and purpose. I encourage every learner to make the most of their journey at GAT and lead with curiosity and compassion.”

The regulations given below enable the college to achieve the goals of achievement testing, 
gain confidence and respect of the stakeholders, particularly students. Typically, 
achievement testin g is done in two parts as follows, both of them being important in 
assessing a student's achievement. 
1.1  Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE):  
Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) to be conducted by the course coordinator all through 
the semester. This incl ude compulsory tests, and alternate assessment tools  (AAT) namely

the semester. This incl ude compulsory tests, and alternate assessment tools  (AAT) namely

1.1.1 Compulsory Tests 
Three internal assessment te sts are conducted by the course coordinator , and the average 
score of three tests along  with the scores obtained in the AAT shall be considered for 
computing the final CIE score of a student in a given course. The internal assessment tests are 
planned by t he Dean Academics in the beginning of the semester and notified to all the 
students. The syllabus for each of the internal assessment test will be around 30 to 40% of

students. The syllabus for each of the internal assessment test will be around 30 to 40% of 
the entire syllabus and the duration of each test is one hour and fifteen minutes. The internal 
assessment test s are conducted as per the academic calendar with a maximum of two 
subjects per day.

attendance in the corresponding course but remained absent for the test due to valid reason. 
One compensatory test will be conducted after the completion of the all the three internal 
assessment tests. However, the committee  constituted by the college will determine the 
validity of the circumstance. Hence, the compensatory test is conducted purely to address 
genuine cases.

Online Education
1. Does all programs/courses were completed on time. Yes

2. Measures taken to complete the syllabus of courses and programs. The global pandemic COVID 19 has brought the world to standstill in all facades and profoundly affected the most underprivileged
disproportionately. All sectors across the globe including education space has seen unprecedented crisis which the world has
ever witnessed and disrupted the teaching-learning ecosystem on an unimaginable scale. Thus, exploring opportunities to
reconstruct the education by making the learning ambience more conducive, shifting from instructional-based approaches to
competency-based approaches especially in the higher education space through online education is a challenging endeavour.

However, online education has shown more maneuverable and acclimatised to respond optimistically to the dynamic aspirations
of the learner. It is also seen to pave way forward for life-long learning. By virtue of rampant expansion to e-learning eco-system,
the digital divide has brought immense challenges to the teaching and learning community. While integrating the e-learning
platforms to enable teaching-learning deliverables, we have truly witnessed issues such as a) lack of tools, b) technical
infrastructure and c) capacity of either community to adopt to the digital framework. This has widened the boundary and created
inequality in quality of delivery and quality of learning.

inequality in quality of delivery and quality of learning.
Despite all the odds, Global Academy of Technology had taken significant measures to foster online education and digitised the
entire teaching-learning process during the unprecedented time. Following are the few well-articulated strategies to manage and
mitigate the risk attributed to the digital divide.
a) All students were given Global Academy of Technology’s domain email in Microsoft platform to bring them into online education
space.
b) Depending on the technical feasibility viz. hardware infrastructure, software infrastructure, online enabling platforms and
internet bandwidth, members of the fraternity were informed to choose the delivery platforms. Microsoft Teams platform, Google

Meet and Zoom Platforms were used to conduct the online classes.
c) Considering the screen access time and students’ retention/stress level, the number of sessions per day had been rationalised
accordingly to minimise the anxiety level among students.
d) Diligent attempts were made to fully automate the Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) components viz Internal Examinations,
Assignments, Surprise Tests and Presentations using the embedded Microsoft Teams products such as Microsoft forms, Virtual
Classrooms through Channels and Google products such as Google Classroom and Google forms. These were imbibed from the
various distinct digital learning initiatives from the Apex bodies such as Swayam, NPTEL etc. Indeed, these endeavours had
yielded splendid results during extraordinary times.

yielded splendid results during extraordinary times.
e) We had also explored blended mode of learning and conducted virtual experiments by exposing the students to various
technology simulation tools which are well appreciated by industry. To augment the virtual experiments, students were instructed
to navigate the URLs viz. https://vlabs.iitkgp.ernet.in, https://de-iitr.vlabs.ac.in and software tools like MATLAB, SIMULINK and
KEIL etc. Apparently, they were suggested to undertake DIY mini projects to improve their technical competencies.
f) To encourage and keeping the enthusiasm, we held various events such as GAT-TECH challenge, STEM Challenge, Musical
compositions, Video book Contest, Skit, Sketch competition, Fiction/non-fiction Poetry competition to augment co-curricular and

extra-curricular activities.

The Women Protection Cell was established to handle workplace sexual harassment

The Women Protection Cell was established to handle workplace sexual harassment 
allegations. The cell improves awareness of women's issues and creates a safe environment 
for them on college campuses. Seminars and guest talks are held to discuss all of the current 
social concerns and how they affect females. The cell is also in charge of investigating 
complaints about women that are made by employees and students regarding the 
institution's female grievances. Students can lodge any grievances they may have i n the 
grievance box located in the girls' common room.  Any complaint is examined, and the cell 
takes the proper action right away. 
Basic Functions of Cell 
• To protect the rights of women and any sorts of violence against them.

Basic Functions of Cell 
• To protect the rights of women and any sorts of violence against them. 
• To effectively address workplace sexual harassment complaints, assure confidentiality, 
and assure non-retaliation.

GAT Undergraduate (B.E.) Eligibility Criteria: Candidates must have passed 10+2 (PUC/CBSE/ICSE or equivalent) with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects along with Chemistry/Biology/Computer Science. A minimum aggregate of 45% (40% for SC/ST/OBC candidates of Karnataka) is required in the qualifying examination. Admission is based on KCET/COMEDK scores or through management quota.

GAT Postgraduate (M.Tech & MBA) Eligibility Criteria: M.Tech candidates must have a B.E./B.Tech degree in a relevant field with a minimum of 50% marks (45% for SC/ST/OBC of Karnataka) and a valid PGCET/GATE score. MBA candidates must have a bachelor's degree (minimum 3 years) with at least 50% marks (45% for SC/ST/OBC of Karnataka) and a valid PGCET/KMAT/CMAT score.

GAT Admission Process: Entrance Exam Route — candidates applying through KCET, COMEDK, PGCET, GATE, KMAT, or CMAT must follow the respective exam authorities' admission process. Management Quota — eligible candidates can apply directly through the college's admission office; selection is based on merit, interview performance, and availability of seats. Lateral Entry (Diploma Holders): admission to the 2nd year of B.E. is through DCET (Diploma CET).

GAT Admission — Required Documents: candidates must fill out the online/offline application form and submit the required documents, including: 10th & 12th mark sheets (or equivalent), entrance exam scorecard (if applicable), Transfer Certificate (TC), Migration Certificate (for non-Karnataka students), Caste Certificate (if applicable), and passport-size photographs.

GAT Scholarships: scholarships are available for meritorious students, economically weaker sections, and reserved category students based on eligibility, including Sports Scholarships for National Level achievers. The exact fee structure is determined as per government regulations and management policies (see the separate fee structure records).
